First public release of **claude-forensics**, a DFIR web tool to ingest and analyse **Claude Code** and **Claude Desktop** artifacts collected from Linux, Windows or macOS workstations.

### Highlights
- **One binary, web UI included:** login-protected, one SQLite database per case.
- **Evidence handling:** drag and drop a ZIP or 7z collection (password-protected archives supported), kept untouched and hashed (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256); every extracted file is hashed, with zip-slip and Windows-name protection.
- **Claude Code:** sessions and full transcripts, tool calls and results, tokens and cost, prompt history (even for deleted sessions), pre-edit file backups, todos, running sessions, OAuth credentials, hooks, permissions and MCP servers.
- **Claude Desktop:** cookie metadata, decoded Local Storage, MCP config, `os_crypt` key, logs.
- **Secret scan:** Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Google, Stripe keys, private keys and JWTs, masked in the UI.
- **Analysis:** super-timeline, full-text search, CSV export protected against formula injection, audit log of reveals and exports.

### Download
| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows x86_64 | [`claude-forensics-windows-x86_64.exe`](https://github.com/Ch4rybd3/claude-forensics/releases/download/v0.1.0/claude-forensics-windows-x86_64.exe) |
| Linux x86_64 | [`claude-forensics-linux-x86_64`](https://github.com/Ch4rybd3/claude-forensics/releases/download/v0.1.0/claude-forensics-linux-x86_64) — `chmod +x` it first |

Quick start: `claude-forensics example-config > claude-forensics.toml`, set a username and password, run `claude-forensics`, then open http://localhost:8080.

Each binary has a `.sha256` checksum next to it. The binaries are not code-signed: Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch ("More info" → "Run anyway").
